title: Morena Accuses Violation of the Secular State Over Award Ceremony for Evangelicals in the Chamber of Deputies
author: Fernando Camacho and Enrique Méndez
content:
_This article by[Fernando Camacho and Enrique
Méndez](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Fernando%20Camacho%20y%20Enrique%20M%C3%A9ndez)
originally appeared in the [October 20, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/20/politica/morena-acusa-
violacion-al-estado-laico-por-acto-religioso-en-san-lazaro), Mexico's premier
left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. The holding of a religious event on Monday in the Chamber of
Deputies, organized by PRI deputy Israel Betanzos and the association Policías
Celestiales (Heavenly Police), which was attended by a representative of the
Israeli embassy, drew rejection from Morena deputies, who considered that it
violated the secular nature of the Mexican State.

In the final part of Tuesday's plenary session, from her seat, legislator
Magdalena Rosales Cruz requested a minute of silence and reproached that “the
situation in Palestine marks three years of intensification of the conflict
since October 2023, a period that various international organizations have
formally described as genocide, with a deliberate focus on attacking children
and destroying the Palestinian population.”

In that context, she emphasized, “yesterday, in this secular chamber of the
Mexican State, the evangelical Christian religious association Policías
Celestiales, which lives by the motto ‘Armed forces at the service of God and
society,’ was received and honored, accompanied by the Israeli embassy.”

The legislator warned that “the relationship between Israel and evangelical
groups, particularly those aligned with so-called Christian Zionism, is a
decisive strategic and geopolitical alliance. The growth of evangelical
communities in the Latin American region has reshaped local politics.”

> In this regard, she added that “the government of Israel has actively
> implemented ‘faith diplomacy,’ tightening diplomatic ties with Latin
> American pastors, religious leaders, and legislators to secure votes and
> support in international forums. It is a symbiotic pact in which Israel
> obtains an unconditional political and financial shield in the West.”

She also noted that Leonel Guillermoprieto is “known as Comandante Chihuahua,
founder of the Policía Celestial association, **arrested in 2007 in the United
States for drug trafficking**. They carry out so-called ‘heavenly operations’
through motivational talks with a religious background in various police
stations around the country.”

She also recalled that “the first records of activity begin in 2015, through
the National Congress of Police at the Service of God and Society. In 2017
they signed their first collaboration agreement with the Special Commission
against Human Trafficking of the Chamber of Deputies and its chair, PRI deputy
Julieta Fernández Márquez, from the state of Guerrero, to give these religious
talks in 10 states of the Republic.”

Fernández Márquez is the wife of the coordinator of the PRI senators, Manuel
Añorve.

> Rosales emphasized that “there have been many martyrs to achieve the
> separation of church and state. Therefore, this secular State, this Chamber
> of Deputies, refuses to accept the continued presence of religious groups in
> this chamber, which is also a tribute to the heroes of the homeland.”

Immediately, her fellow party member Beatriz Navarro joined in to “expose the
unprecedented event” convened on Monday by PRI deputy Israel Betanzos, when,
she cited, **Article 40 of the Constitution establishes that Mexico is a
secular State**.

> That is why we cannot allow its facilities to be used for political and
> religious events of particular groups. I want to correct myself: perhaps for
> political events, yes, but religious ones, never! Our Constitution is
> respected and must be inviolable.
>
> Deputy Beatriz Navarro

Navarro complained that the organization of police officers, both retired and
active, had given awards to opposition mayors “and to the Israeli embassy, who
are genocidal, since they have killed more than 74,000 Palestinians and
wounded more than 175,000 residents of Gaza in less than three years. This
only reflects their inhumanity and what they are: genocidal.”

Giving them an award, she added, “is an offense to the memory of the victims
and to the dignity that this Chamber should represent. No one denies them
their right to meet and to think as they wish, but do it somewhere else. This
space is not yours: it belongs to the people of Mexico and it is for the
defense of human rights.”

## **PAZ Operative at the Meeting**

Separately, in an interview with this newspaper, the deputy coordinator of the
Morena caucus, Dolores Padierna Luna, alluded, without mentioning her name, to
Morena deputy Carolina Anda González, who was also present at Monday's award
ceremony, and considered that she acted against the support her party has
expressed for Palestine and its people.

“This Morena deputy who was there is the alternate of Hugo Éric (Flores,
current leader of the PAZ). They operate with religious matters and don't
quite understand that this doesn't go with politics. We all have freedom of
worship, but we cannot violate the Constitution in this Chamber,” she said.

Anda González is identified as a financial operative of the PAZ, the third
party created by Hugo Éric Flores, and is also one of the people closest to
the Morelos lawyer.

Padierna said there are deputies who do not want to accept Morena's political
line, “who put on the cap of citizens or unions or civil society when Morena's
political line doesn't suit them. And they are Morena members for electoral
purposes and for other things.

“So I would say that Morena, the Honesty and Justice Commission, has to
enforce the political line set by our national councils. We don't act on our
own; we have a political line to respect, and it must be respected by
everyone.”

## **Secular State, Not Jacobin: PRI**

In the morning, the coordinator of the PRI deputies, Rubén Moreira, defended
Monday's event, backed his fellow party member Israel Betanzos, and denied
that it had been an affront to the secular State.

> “I did not see a liturgical act, I saw a ceremony in which some awards were
> given, and of course (Betanzos) has the support of our caucus. The Chamber
> must be open to all kinds of things,” he cut in during an interview.

—Isn't the secular nature of the State affected?

—Secular is one thing and Jacobin is another. The secular State is not
affected by that; it is affected when decisions are made that are removed from
science, from democracy. When public decisions are made like those (former
President Andrés Manuel) López Obrador made, those of the “detente” (in
reference to a religious image, during the Covid pandemic). That is where
there is a problem with the secular State,” he argued.

—Doesn't it give a bad image because of the genocide against the Palestinian
people? he was pressed.

—This is a place where ambassadors from all countries are welcome, and I don't
think it is a place for us to question that. We must remember that the conduct
of the Mexican State in international matters corresponds to the head of the
Mexican State.

When asked why the PRI invited Leonel Guillermoprieto to the chamber, despite
his criminal record in Mexico and the United States, he replied: “I don't know
him.”
